# Current State Audit

GENERATED FILE — `node scripts/execution/generate-current-state-audit.mjs`.
Do not hand-edit. Edit `docs/execution/section-assessments.json` and regenerate.

## Why this file is generated

The §84 checklist tracked in `docs/exec/EXECUTION_STATUS.md` was transcribed by
hand. It carried 60 of the specification’s 68 Definition-of-Done items, and the
eight it omitted were invisible **because** they were omitted — nothing
downstream can ask about a row that does not exist. One of them, "all 195
baseline countries present exactly once", stayed invisible while three
destinations were built on top of it.

So the section list below is read out of the specification at generation time.
A section cannot go missing from this audit. It can only be assessed, or
printed as `NOT_ASSESSED` — which is a true statement about what we know,
rather than a blank row that reads as nothing to worry about.

The specification currently has **89** numbered sections.

## Status tally

| Status | Sections |
|---|---|
| `VERIFIED_COMPLETE` | 72 |
| `PARTIAL` | 13 |
| `BLOCKED` | 4 |
| **Total** | **89** |

## Vocabulary

§0.1 defines exactly six statuses and the generator rejects anything else:
`VERIFIED_COMPLETE`, `IMPLEMENTED_NOT_VERIFIED`, `PARTIAL`, `NOT_STARTED`,
`BLOCKED`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`. `NOT_ASSESSED` is added here for sections nobody
has looked at yet, because calling those `NOT_STARTED` would assert knowledge
we do not have — the work may well be done.

`NOT_APPLICABLE` requires a justification in the evidence column. §0.1 is
explicit that it must never be used merely to reduce scope.
